summary: A personal RSS reader that is polite to the sites it reads: your Feedly OPML imported with folders, conditional fetching so unchanged feeds cost nothing, dedupe that survives rotating GUIDs, sanitized content, a keyboard-driven reader, starred items and full-text search, and optional LLM summaries that only appear when a key exists.

stack.why: a reader UI and a fetch loop in one process
battle-tested feed parsing; scheduling without a queue
full text over everything you have read, no service
your reading list is nobody's business

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: Your Feedly OPML export
prerequisites.why: Phase 1 imports it so nothing is retyped.
prerequisites.get: Feedly > Settings (gear) > OPML > Export. Save it as feeds.opml in the project.

prerequisites.name: A User-Agent string with a contact URL
prerequisites.why: Polite fetching identifies itself. Site owners can reach you if your reader misbehaves.

prerequisites.name: An LLM API key (optional)
prerequisites.why: Phase 6 adds a per-article summary button; without a key the button does not exist.

env.name: OPML_PATH
env.where: Your subscription list; the reader exports back to it.

env.name: USER_AGENT
env.where: Identifies your fetcher to the sites you read.

env.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
env.where: Enables summaries. Empty hides the feature entirely.

phases.title: OPML and feed list
phases.goal: Import with folders, idempotently, and export back.

steps.do: Create the project and the tables
steps.detail: feeds (id, url, title, folder, site_url, etag, last_modified, last_fetched_at, last_status, consecutive_failures, disabled), items (id, feed_id, guid, link, title, author, published_at, content, read, starred, fetched_at), unique (feed_id, guid).
commands: mkdir reader && cd reader && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module
npm install express@4 better-sqlite3@13 rss-parser@3 node-cron@3

steps.do: Import OPML preserving folders; export on demand

check: A real Feedly OPML imports with folders intact
Re-importing adds nothing
The export re-imports into an identical tree

phases.title: Polite fetching
phases.goal: Conditional GETs, a real User-Agent, timeouts, per-host courtesy, backoff.

steps.do: Send If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since; handle 304 by doing nothing
steps.detail: Skipping this re-downloads every feed forever, which is how a reader becomes a nuisance.

steps.do: Set USER_AGENT, a timeout, per-host concurrency of 1 with a delay
Back off failing feeds and disable after enough failures

check: A second fetch of an unchanged feed returns 304 and writes nothing
A feed returning 500 backs off
A timeout does not delay the others
Malformed XML is logged without killing the loop

phases.title: Item ingestion
phases.goal: Dedupe that survives bad GUIDs, and HTML that cannot hurt you.

steps.do: Dedupe by guid, fall back to link, treat a rotating guid as absent
Sanitize content against an allowlist, strip tracking pixels, absolutize URLs

check: Refetching produces zero new items
A feed with rotating guids does not duplicate
A script tag in content is stripped
A relative image renders correctly

phases.title: Reader UI
phases.goal: Folders with counts, a list, a reading pane, keyboard everything.

steps.do: Build the three panes: folder tree with unread counts, article list, reading pane
Add keyboard shortcuts j/k/o/m/s/A and dark mode
steps.detail: Mark-as-read on scroll-past is a preference, not the default.

check: Unread counts stay correct through every action
Keyboard focus survives list re-renders
A 5,000-item list scrolls without lag

phases.title: Starred and search

steps.do: Add an FTS5 table over titles and content, synced by triggers

check: Search finds a phrase inside an article body
Deleting an item removes it from the index

phases.title: Optional summaries
phases.goal: A button that exists only when a key does, cached per item.

steps.do: Render the summarize button only when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set
steps.detail: A dead button is worse than no button.

steps.do: Cache the summary on the item so reopening does not re-bill

check: With no key there is no trace of the feature
With a key a summary generates once and is reused

phases.title: Retention and deploy
phases.goal: Prune read items, keep starred, back up, run as a service.

steps.do: Nightly prune of read items older than 90 days, never starred
Nightly backup, a systemd unit, and the README
steps.detail: README: how to add a feed (edit the OPML) and export it back, the polite-fetching behaviour as a promise, where the database lives.

check: Pruning never deletes a starred item
Unread counts survive a restart

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the reader is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.
Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: A reader you could run for a few people on your network: polite by construction, searchable for years, with summaries as a paid-key extra.

architecture.swap: Any list format producing the same rows

operations.restore: Copy back; unread counts and stars are in the file.
operations.monitoring: Alert if the fetch loop has not run in an hour.
operations.incident: If a site complains, disable the feed and check your User-Agent and interval.

releaseGate: 304 handling verified against a real feed
Sanitizer verified against a hostile fixture

notIncluded: Mobile apps; the web UI over your network is the answer.
Feed discovery and their AI filtering layer, which need a crawl of the web.
after: A read-later inbox that saves arbitrary URLs into the same reader
